details.biography:
The Broken Anvil · Level 1 - The Apprentices · Seat 4, Ranged

A theatrical tiefling who signed a clever little contract with Glasya, Princess of Hell, to wriggle out of a much worse one. Has never once been patient: sardonic, dramatic and quietly terrified of the voice that answers when she whispers. Glasya got her out of a debt-binding; the Keepers were the first people in Tariel who didn't ask about the horns.

In a fight

Stay at the back and Eldritch Blast every turn (Reflex DC 14: 1d6+3 on a failed save, half of 1d6 on a success), save Sleep for a knot of goblins, and turn invisible when it all goes wrong.
details.backgroundStory:
Abilities (from the printed sheet)

Eldritch Blast. At-will cantrip, 60ft, one target: Reflex save DC 14. On a failure, 1d6 force +3 (Cantrip Mastery); on a success, half of 1d6 with no bonus. Never uses a slot.

Spell Use. Arcane caster, Charisma-based, save DC 14. 2 1st-level slots a day (1 + 1 for Cha 18), refreshed by a long rest. You know two 1st-level spells: Burning Hands (Path spell) and Sleep. No spell attack rolls: harmful spells always call for a save. Damage taken while casting forces a Fortitude save (DC 10 or half the damage) or the spell is lost.

Hellfire Affinity (Infernal Path). Resistance 5 to fire damage. Treat every 1 on your fire damage dice as a 2 (Burning Hands, Fiendish Retort).

Dark Gift: Glasya's Veil. Once a day, as your action, become Invisible for 1 minute (10 rounds). It ends only if you attack or cast an offensive spell, not when you open doors or handle objects. While Invisible, attacks against you have Disadvantage and you cannot be seen without magic or special senses.

Tiefling. Medium size, speed 30ft, darkvision 60ft.

Fire Resistance. Resistance 5 to fire (the same 5 as Hellfire Affinity; they do not add up).

Infernal Cantrip. One Warlock cantrip at creation: Ghost Sound.

Fiendish Retort. Once per long rest, when a creature within 30ft damages you, hit it back as part of your action on your next turn for 1d6 fire (1s count as 2s). No save is listed.

Cantrip Mastery (Arcane & Devout, Warlock 1st-level feat). Learn two extra cantrips (Mage Hand, Message). Once per round, when a cantrip you cast hits or its target fails its save, add your Charisma modifier (+3) to its damage. Does not stack with Agonising Blast.

Notes. Speed: 30ft · Initiative: +1 · HP: d6 max (6) + Con mod (+2) = 8. Untrained NWPs are rolled with Disadvantage; everyday checks (notice, climb, intimidate) are plain attribute checks.

Casting

Every spell is resolved by the target's save against your DC. Tick a slot box when you cast; slots return after a full rest. Cantrips are cast at will. Tick the circle beside a spell to mark it prepared.

Eldritch Blast (cantrip): 60ft, one target: Reflex DC 14. Failed save 1d6+3 force; success half of 1d6. At will. The +3 is Cantrip Mastery, added only when the target fails its save.

Ghost Sound (cantrip, Infernal Cantrip): 30ft, 1 round: a sound as loud as up to 4 shouting people (footsteps, a growl, clashing arms) from a point you choose. No words. No save.

Mage Hand (cantrip, Cantrip Mastery): 30ft, 1 minute: an invisible hand moves one unattended object of up to 5 lb at 15ft a round. Cannot attack or force anything.

Message (cantrip, Cantrip Mastery): 120ft, one creature, 10 minutes: whisper a message only it hears; it can whisper back. Blocked by 1ft of stone, 1 inch of metal or silence.

Burning Hands (1st, Path spell): 15ft cone from your hands: 1d3+1 fire (1s count as 2s), Reflex halves. Ignites unattended flammable objects. Noisy and bright.

Sleep (1st): 90ft, 15ft radius: creatures totalling 2d4+1 Levels fall Unconscious for 1d4 minutes, lowest Level first; Level 5+ unaffected. Will negates. Damage wakes a sleeper. Undead and constructs are immune.

Armour Class on the sheet: 10 + 1 (Dex); no armour or shield (Warlocks are trained in none, and wearing any blocks casting) = 11

Class Abilities

1st Level

Eldritch Blast

  • Effect: At-will ranged cantrip (60ft range). The target makes a Reflex save (DC = 10 + half your Warlock level (minimum 1) + Cha modifier), taking force damage on a failure or half on a success. No slot required.
  • Damage scales: 1d6 at 1st, 1d8 at 5th, 2d6 at 9th, 2d8 at 13th, 3d6 at 17th, 3d8 at 24th

Spell Use

  • Effect: Cast arcane spells using your slots. Each time you unlock a slot level you gain two spells of that level: your Path spell (see Patron Paths) and one spell of your choice from the Warlock list in Spellcasting in Arneyan. You may cast any spell you know with any slot of its level or higher. Slots are shared with Pact Summons — see Spell Slot Progression above.

Dark Gift

  • Effect: A passive benefit granted by your specific patron Kit. See the Patron Paths section for details. A Dark Gift that adds damage or defence works only while your Warlock level is at least half your character level.

2nd Level

Eldritch Invocations

  • Effect: Choose one invocation from the list below. Choose another at 5th, 9th, 13th and 17th level. You cannot take the same invocation twice.
  • Agonising Blast: add your Charisma modifier to Eldritch Blast damage.
  • Repelling Blast: a creature of Large size or smaller hit by Eldritch Blast is pushed 10ft.
  • Armour of Shadows: +2 AC while you wear no armour and carry no shield (+3 from 10th level). Does not stack with other unarmoured bonuses of the same kind.
  • Fiendish Vigour: once per day, as part of your action, gain temporary hit points equal to your Warlock level. They last until your next long rest.
  • Mask of Many Faces: cast Change Self at will.
  • Devil's Sight: see normally in darkness, magical or otherwise, to 60ft.

3rd Level

Pact Summons

  • Effect: Your patron sends a servant. Every summons expends a slot of the creature's tier (Tier 1 = 1st level, Tier 2 = 2nd, Tier 3 = 3rd). A ritual summons takes 10 minutes and lasts 1 hour; a combat summons uses your action and lasts 1 minute. Full stat blocks are in Monsters & Treasure. Tier 1 servants have double the HP and damage dice of their stat blocks, and the table below already shows them doubled.
  • The creature does not roll initiative: it acts immediately after you each round, moving and taking one action (all its listed attacks together count as that action). It obeys your spoken commands; with none, it attacks the nearest visible enemy
  • One summon active at a time. It departs when its duration ends, when you dismiss it with a word or when slain; a slain summon cannot be called again until you finish a long rest
  • If you fall unconscious, your summon only defends itself until you wake or it departs

6th Level

  • Patron's Mark: a minor ability from your patron. Defined by your Kit

12th Level

  • Patron Feature: a stronger active ability from your patron. Defined by your Kit

15th Level

Pact Summons (Tier 4)

  • Effect: Your patron's most powerful servant becomes available. Tier 4 summons expend a 5th level slot, whether ritual or combat.

Dark Harvest

  • Effect: Once per encounter, when you reduce a creature to 0 HP or below, recover one expended spell slot of a level up to half that creature's Level (rounded up, minimum 1st level). It must be a hostile creature that attacked you or an ally this encounter and was not Restrained, Paralysed, Unconscious or otherwise helpless, and never one summoned, created or controlled by you or your allies.
  • Example: kill a Level 6 creature, recover up to a 3rd level slot
  • Charisma Bonus: gain a permanent +1 to Charisma. This increases the DC of your spells and abilities, and all Charisma-based checks

20th Level

Patron Surge

  • Effect: Once per day, cast a spell one level above your current maximum. You take 1d6 unavoidable damage per level of the surge — this cannot be reduced by any means.
  • At 20th level your maximum is 6th level. Choose one 7th-level Wizard spell as your Patron Surge: once per day you can cast it without a slot, taking 7d6 damage yourself. The patron's power always has a price

Patron's Whisper

  • Effect: Once per day, commune directly with your patron to ask one yes/no question. The answer is always truthful — though the patron's understanding of truth may not align with yours.

24th Level

Eldritch Master

  • Effect: Once per day, spend 1 minute communing with your patron to immediately recover all expended spell slots. The patron always wants something in return — the GM determines the cost narratively.

Patron Paths

Each kit is an item in the Kits compendium, in the Warlock folder. Drag one onto your character.

  • Choose a Path at character creation. Each Path grants a passive, its own base spell list, and a shared summon pool. Kits within each Path define your Dark Gift, Patron's Mark, and Patron Feature.

Path of the Infernal

The Nine Hells run on hierarchy, contracts, and hellfire. Every devil serves the chain above them. Every Infernal Warlock serves that chain whether they know it or not.

  • Path Passive — Hellfire Affinity: Resistance 5 to fire damage. Treat all 1s on fire damage dice as 2s.

Path Spells

  • One Path spell per slot level, gained when that slot level is unlocked (alongside your chosen Warlock-list spell of the same level). Cast it with any slot of that level or higher; a Path spell is always treated as the slot level shown in the table, even where the Master list gives it a different level. Slots are shared with summoning — a slot spent on a summon cannot also be used to cast.

"Tiefling" is what others call them. A tiefling is born into a family of another ancestry, human, orc, elf or any other, whose bloodline carries a fiendish curse. The mark can skip generations and appear in a child of ordinary-looking parents. There is no tiefling people, homeland or culture.

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Cha / +1 Int, −1 Wis

Traits

  • Family: choose the ancestry of the family you were born into. You speak its language, and others treat you as one of its people once they look past the marks. Your size, speed, vision and traits are the Tiefling's, whatever your family.
  • Resistance 5 to a damage type set by your bloodline.
  • One Warlock cantrip at creation.
  • Fiendish Retort: 1/long rest, when damaged by a creature within 30ft, unleash it back at them as part of your action on your next turn. The damage type is set by your bloodline: 1d6 at 1st, 1d8 at 5th, 2d6 at 9th, 2d8 at 13th, 3d6 at 17th, 3d8 at 24th.
  • From 11th level, Fiendish Retort can be used twice per long rest.

Bloodlines

  • Infernal (devils): horns, a tail, embers in the eyes. Resist fire; Retort deals fire. Advantage on checks to read, recall or find loopholes in contracts, oaths and bargains. You know Infernal.
  • Abyssal (demons): wild, twisted features that rarely look the same twice in a family. Resist poison; Retort deals acid. Advantage on Charisma checks to intimidate. You know Abyssal.
  • Outer (daemons, rakshasa and stranger fiends): subtle, unsettling marks that are hard to place. Resist necrotic; Retort deals necrotic. Advantage on checks to see through disguises and illusions. You know Infernal or Abyssal.
  • Shadowfell (fiends of shadow): ashen skin, a shadow that moves a moment late. Resist cold; Retort deals cold. Advantage on checks to hide in dim light or darkness. You know Infernal or Abyssal.
